title: Citrate Utilization Test
principle: Tests whether an organism can use citrate as its sole carbon source. Utilization raises the medium's pH (via byproducts of citrate metabolism), which shifts a pH indicator (commonly bromothymol blue) from green to Prussian blue.
purpose: Part of the IMViC panel; helps distinguish citrate-positive organisms (e.g. many Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter species) from citrate-negative organisms (e.g. most E. coli strains) among Enterobacteriaceae.
reagents: Simmons Citrate Agar (see media entry; citrate as sole carbon source, with bromothymol blue indicator)

procedure.instruction: Lightly inoculate a Simmons Citrate Agar slant by streaking the surface with a needle/loop — do not stab deeply, since this test relies on aerobic surface growth.
Incubate at the appropriate temperature/duration for the organism, leaving the cap slightly loose to permit aeration.
Observe the slant for growth and color change.

positiveResult: Visible growth on the slant accompanied by a color change from green to Prussian/royal blue.
negativeResult: No growth and no color change (medium remains green).
interpretation: A positive result indicates the organism can use citrate as its sole carbon source under these conditions; color change without visible growth, or growth without full color change, should be interpreted cautiously and, where relevant, is one part of a larger identification workflow rather than a standalone answer.
precautions: Use a light surface inoculation, not a heavy stab, to avoid a false reading from anaerobic conditions deep in the slant.
limitations: A very heavy inoculum can occasionally cause a color change through carryover of nutrients rather than true citrate utilization — inoculate lightly with a fresh, isolated colony.
